chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed the Quran is a prohibitor and a commander — it commands toward Paradise and prohibits from the Fire.'

key_terms.آمِرٌ: Commander/orderer — one who actively directs and enjoins toward good
key_terms.النَّار: The Fire — Hell, the consequence warned against by the Quran
key_terms.الْجَنَّة: Paradise — the ultimate reward for those who follow the Quran's commands
key_terms.زَاجِرٌ: Prohibitor/restrainer — one who actively deters and prevents from wrongdoing

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the function of the Quran?
ai.summary: Abu Basir reports that Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) described the dual function of the Quran: it simultaneously commands believers toward Paradise and prohibits them from the Fire. This teaching was addressed to the Imam's close companions who transmitted his teachings on the Quran's living, active guidance. The statement reflects the Shia understanding of the Quran as a dynamic guide that actively steers its followers, not merely a passive text.
